title: This Lake Didn't Exist in Early 2020
sources: Every fact comes from episodes/gerd-nile (fact-checked there, see its research.md and script.json).

Before/after: Copernicus Sentinel-2 L2A, least cloudy scenes 2020-01-15..2020-03-31 vs 2026-02-01..2026-03-31 (same windows as the long episode). The first filling began in July 2020, so early 2020 had no reservoir.
Reservoir about 1,874 km2 at full supply level; Greater London 1,572 km2. Main dam 145 m tall. GERD is Africa's biggest hydropower plant (5,150 MW).
Egypt: 'existential threat'. Ethiopia: 'not a threat, but a shared opportunity' (prime minister at the inauguration, 9 Sep 2025).
About 85% of the Nile water that reaches Egypt comes from the Ethiopian highlands (Blue Nile plus Atbara and Sobat; FAO, Nile Basin research).
The lake reached its full level (640 m) in late 2024 and was full at the inauguration; the Feb-Mar 2026 Sentinel-2 scenes show it full.

paragraphs.text: Western Ethiopia, early 2020. Now, the same valley six years later.
A brand-new lake, bigger than all of Greater London. Holding it back, a concrete wall a hundred and forty-five metres tall: the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam.
Downstream, Egypt has called this dam an existential threat. Ethiopia calls it a shared opportunity.
Why does that worry Egypt? About eighty-five percent of the Nile water that reaches Egypt starts in the Ethiopian highlands.

shots.on_screen_text: About 85% of Egypt's Nile water starts in Ethiopia

paragraphs.text: The lake is full now. So, which is it: a threat, or an opportunity? Tell me what you think.

youtube.description:
The same valley in western Ethiopia, early 2020 and six years later, in real Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite images: the new lake behind the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) on the Blue Nile.

Full documentary: https://youtu.be/bR4wVyHqct4
